articles.title: Fast X-Ray Transients from Dense Circumstellar Material Shock Breakout and Cooling Emission
articles.abstract: In this Letter, we explore the soft X-ray shock breakout (SBO) and cooling emission of supernovae interacting with pre-explosion dense circumstellar material (CSM) shells as a subclass of extragalactic fast X-ray transients. For geometrically thin CSM shells, we find that the SBO luminosities span a range of a few $10^{43}-10^{45}\,{\rm{erg}}\,{\rm{s}}^{-1}$, with peak times typically $\lesssim10^4\,{\rm{s}}$, both of which are primarily determined by the light-travel effect. When the shell's outer radius is located at $\sim100-500\,R_\odot$, the SBO temperatures fall into the energy band covered by the current soft X-ray facilities. We derive analytic lightcurves for SBOs in dense CSM shells and explore how different physical parameters affect the observed lightcurves and the temperature evolution. Despite the multi-temperature nature of the emission caused by the light-travel effect leading to non-thermal-like spectra, we find that the time-resolved spectra within the limited soft X-ray band can still be well described by a blackbody model. This provides a natural explanation for the observed blackbody-like time-resolved spectra of soft X-ray SBO events. Our model can reproduce the observed X-ray lightcurves and temperature evolutions of the three known X-ray SBO events, EP260321a, XRF\,060218, and XRO\,080109, revealing a diversity in the properties of the dense CSM shells ejected by stripped-envelope progenitors before the explosion. Future discoveries of more soft X-ray SBO events by facilities such as Einstein Probe will provide opportunities for probing the episodic mass-loss history of massive stars in the final stages before core collapse.

articles.title: SN 2017gkk: A moderately luminous and fast evolving Type IIb supernova
articles.abstract: We present optical imaging (\textit{BVRI} bands) and low-resolution optical spectroscopic follow-up of Type IIb supernova SN~2017gkk that occurred in NGC~2748. These observations consist of 31 and 17 epochs of photometry and spectroscopy, spanning $\sim$\,218 days since the $V$-band peak. The light curve analysis infers that the SN reached maximum in $\sim$\,13~days after the explosion with an absolute magnitude of $M_\mathrm{V}$\,=\,--17.01\,$\pm$\,0.07 mag. The peak pseudo-bolometric luminosity of SN~2017gkk is $L_{\rm bol}=(8.37\pm0.19)\times10^{41}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Between 25 and 80 days (after maximum), SN~2017gkk displays a fast decline rate of $2.35\pm0.06~\mathrm{mag\times(100d)^{-1}}$ in $V$-band. The photospheric phase spectra are dominated by an H$α$ P~Cygni profile (up to $\sim$\,69~days), which gradually faded and disappeared $\sim$\,90 days after the $V$-band maximum. The \ion{He}{1} lines subsequently emerged after $\sim$\,20 days and became dominant during the transition phase. The nebular phase spectra of SN~2017gkk indicate a relatively low-mass progenitor with $M_{\mathrm{preSN}}\gtrsim3\,M_\odot$ and $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}}\approx\,12\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, and it is likely in a binary system. The analytical modeling of the light curve infers a low ejecta mass of $M_{\mathrm{ej}}=1.38^{+0.48}_{-0.31}\, M_\odot$ with relatively lower explosion energy $E_\mathrm{KE}=0.69_{-0.17}^{+0.25}\times10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$ and a synthesized $^{56}$Ni mass of $M_{\mathrm{Ni}}=0.076_{-0.024}^{+0.032}\, M_\odot$.

articles.title: Design and Forecasts for a Rubin Twilight Program for Nearby Type Ia Supernovae
articles.abstract: Nearby Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are important for supernova cosmology, but saturation in 30 s exposures, gaps in light-curve sampling, and the footprint of Vera C. Rubin Observatory's baseline Wide-Fast-Deep (WFD) survey limit the nearby sample. To improve the low-$z$ sample, we propose a twilight follow-up program using Rubin Observatory for 1-5 s griz exposures at solar altitudes $-12^\circ \le \mathrm{Alt}_\odot \le -9^\circ$. Using simulations of one year of WFD observations, we find that twilight follow-up adds 230 quality-selected SNe Ia from an external sample drawn primarily from the Transient Name Server (TNS). At $z<0.08$, the usable sample increases from 368 to 643 SNe Ia, including 50 WFD events recovered by refitting their light curves with twilight photometry. Combining these twilight observations with high-redshift WFD and Deep Drilling Field samples increases the statistical-only dark-energy $(w_0,w_a)$ figure of merit from 49.3 to 58.3 (18%) and reduces $σ(w_a)$ by 10%. For measurements of structure growth at $0.02 \le z<0.06$, the fractional uncertainty on $fσ_8$ decreases from 0.783 to 0.305. Restricting the program to $-12^\circ \le \mathrm{Alt}_\odot \le -11^\circ$ reduces the dark-energy improvement to 7.2%. These short exposures could also provide unsaturated photometry of potential distance-ladder calibrators at $z<0.02$.
authors: the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration

articles.title: The Silk Nebula Revisited: A Comment on Wu et al. (2026) and New Constraints from Archival Survey Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Wu et al. (2026) used one LAMOST MRS-N plate to suggest that the Silk Nebula, a $17^\circ$-long \Oiii~$λ$5007 filament in Gemini, is possibly associated with a supernova remnant at a fiducial distance of $\sim$160\,pc. We test this against their published values and independent archival data. The \Ni\ airglow in their blue-arm spectrum lies at air, topocentric rest wavelengths, so their \Oiii\ velocities omit the heliocentric correction and are $10.1\pm1.0$\,\kms\ too high. Corrected and combined with DESI DR1 and SDSS spectra, \Oiii\ lies at \vhel\ $=+13.3\pm1.0$\,\kms, the velocity of \Nii\ and of the local warm ionized medium (WIM). Their \Ha\ velocities are 4.5--6.7\,\kms\ redder than \Nii. Their tabulated distances are in kpc, not units of 100\,pc, and kinematic distances carry no information in this direction. Their surface brightness exceeds independent measurements (1.4--2.5 rayleighs) by factors of 4.6--8.6. Their red-line shock criteria are met equally in their nebula-free background region and describe the WIM; their other remnant diagnostics do not constrain the filament. DESI and SDSS spectra show that the filament is Balmer-dark (\Oiii/\Hb\ $>11$) and \Oii-strong, with \ion{He}{2}/\Oiii\ $<0.026$; GALEX shows a coincident ultraviolet ridge, with no \Ha, \ion{H}{1}, dust or X-ray counterpart. These properties, and the lack of an ionizing source, exclude photoionization equilibrium and complete radiative shocks and match a column-truncated radiative shock of $\sim$80--120\,\kms\ seen edge-on, plausibly on the limb of the Monogem Ring at $\sim$250--320\,pc. Far-ultraviolet and deep optical spectroscopy, a two-epoch proper motion and high-ion absorption toward bracketing white dwarfs would be decisive.

articles.title: Superoutburst Precursors in the Faint SU UMa-type Dwarf Nova KSP-OT-201602a
articles.abstract: We present the discovery and photometric study of an SU UMa-type dwarf nova (DN) KSP-OT-201602a. Korea Microlensing Telescope Network Supernova Program data covered almost four years from 2016 to 2019 in BVI-bands for this field, and discovered this faint SU UMa-type DN. Two superoutbursts (SOs: S1 and S2) and two normal outbursts (NOs: N1 and N2) are observed of which peak brightnesses are V = 18.95 mag (S1), V = 18.69 mag (S2) and V = 19.37 mag (N1), V = 19.11 mag (N2). The phase dispersion minimization analysis on superhump of S1 gives the superhump period of 1.52 hr (= 91.2 minutes = 0.06333 days). The magnitude amplitudes for the SOs are 4.34 mag (S1) and 4.60 mag (S2), and those for the NOs are 3.98 mag (N1) and 4.18 mag (N2). The durations of the SOs are 11.39 days (S1) and 12.00 days (S2), and those for the NOs are 2.68 days (N1) and 3.38 days (N2). Clear evidence of a precursor is identified in S1 before the SO peak and this supports the hypothesis that precursor is an NO triggerring an SO and the superhump, while a potential precursor based on limited data is only observed in S2. While the amplitudes of the SOs appear typical for SU UMa-type DNe, their durations seem to be quite short which might require further model calculations in the future.

articles.title: Near Infrared HST Images Resolve the Filamentary Emission Knots in Pa 30, the Remnant of the Galactic Supernova of 1181 AD
articles.abstract: We report the results of a near-infrared HST WFC3/IR imaging program investigating the sub-arcsecond structure of optical filaments in the Galactic nebula, Pa 30, believed to be a SNIax remnant of the historic supernova of 1181 AD. Using a near infrared filter sensitive to [S II] and [S III] emission lines, a 1.2 micron filter to reject stars, and a deep Gemini GMOS [S II] image to help define the remnant's filaments, we identify 226 knots along radially aligned filaments in 15 fields. Knot median PSF-corrected FWHM is 0.154'' (350 AU at 2.3 kpc) with 32 (14%) unresolved at a PSF of 0.225''. We find that Pa 30's knots are not round but elongated along the filaments. Fitting stacks of knots with their axes aligned to their filament directions and calibrating with artificial knots gives intrinsic sizes of 0.18'' along and 0.11'' across filaments, with about 75% of knots longer when measured along the filament. The minimum nearest-neighbor spacing of knots along a filament is typically 0.6'' (1400 AU) so several times their own size, but can be one-arcsecond or larger in places. This results in 5'' to 15'' long discontinuous chains of separate clumps rather than a continuous structure. We find excellent agreement with recent ground-based Gemini images of Pa 30 when HST images are blurred to the 0.5'' Gemini PSF and conclude that filamentary knots detected in Gemini data are actually blurred HST resolved knots. Finally, we give estimates on the density and mass of sulfur in these knots, set an upper limit on their [Fe II] 1.257 micron flux, and briefly discuss implications for modeling the formation of the remnant's filaments.

articles.title: The gravitational wave candidate S251112cm: near-complete optical coverage with ATLAS, Pan-STARRS and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
articles.abstract: On 2025 November 12, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) network detected S251112cm, a compact binary merger candidate with a false alarm rate of one per four years at a luminosity distance of $93 \pm 27$ Mpc. The probability that the lighter component's mass lies below 1 $M_\odot$ is >99%, while the probability that either component lies at 1-3 $M_\odot$ is only 8%, leaving the nature of the progenitor system unclear. We present Pan-STARRS and ATLAS optical follow-up of the 90% localisation region, and quantify Vera C. Rubin Observatory target-of-opportunity observations. In the North, Pan-STARRS imaged 1084 deg$^2$ (65%) within 7 days to a median depth of 21.9 mag and ATLAS 1545 deg$^2$ (87%) within 14 days to 19.3 mag across both hemispheres; in the South, Rubin covered 849 deg$^2$ (36%) 2-10 days post-merger to median depths of 24.5 ($g$) and 23.5 ($i$) mag. They reported 173, 93 and 67 candidates respectively (269 unique), which we assess against AT 2017gfo-like kilonova and SN 1998bw-like broad-lined Type Ic supernova models using prior activity, host luminosity distance, photometric evolution and absolute magnitude. Eight survive, mainly for lack of distance information. Six of these lie in hosts fainter than any in a volume-limited comparison sample, suggesting they are background sources. AT 2025aimy declines too slowly for the AT 2017gfo-like model, and a VLT host spectrum places AT 2025alqe outside the LVK volume, leaving no convincing counterpart candidates. Pan-STARRS and Rubin together exclude both models in $\sim$80% of the 90% localisation volume: the deepest wide-area constraint on a subsolar-mass merger to date and, to our knowledge, the most complete optical coverage of a significant subsolar-mass candidate.

articles.title: Spatio-Temporal Evolution of a Steady Transition Region Downflow above a Sunspot
articles.abstract: Super-Sonic Downflows (SSDs) are usually observed above sunspots as redshifted peaks in lower Transition Region (TR) spectral lines and can last from a few minutes to several hours. Utilising high-cadence, $\sim$3 hour long repeated-raster mode observations from Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS), we investigate the spatio-temporal dynamics of such a downflow event above NOAA active region 12135. Triple Gaussian fitting to TR spectral lines, along with Non-Force Free Field (NFFF) extrapolation and Differential Emission Measure (DEM) analysis, is performed to study this event. Downflow is initially observed in both the umbral and penumbral regions. Over time, the penumbral downflow fades, while the umbral downflow strengthens and appears as a single structure initially but eventually splits into two spatial segments. The calculated average properties, including downflow speed, electron density, and mass flux for this event, align with established studies. Simultaneous evolution in overlying coronal loops is also observed using imaging data from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA). DEM analysis of the coronal emission over the downflow region indicates corresponding changes in cool ($\log_{10}[T/\mathrm{K}] \in [5.5, 5.6]$) coronal plasma. As suggested by recurrent transient brightenings observed in the nearby region in coronal channels and the corresponding fan-spine magnetic topology identified from NFFF extrapolations, magnetic reconnection occurring in this region is proposed to be the cause of this evolution. Our analysis revealed that changes in the morphology of TR downflows are closely associated with evolution of overlying coronal loops.

articles.title: Gamma-Ray Bursts from Primordial Black Hole-Induced Neutron Star Collapse
articles.abstract: We show that the capture and subsequent endoparasitic consumption of a neutron star (NS) by a primordial black hole (PBH) can produce a short gamma-ray burst (GRB) without forming an accretion disk. During PBH-induced NS consumption, the NS spin is amplified through angular-momentum conservation and transfer from infalling matter, while flux freezing and a differential-rotation-driven dynamo amplify the magnetic field. We find that, for rapidly rotating millisecond pulsars (MSPs), these mechanisms can power short GRBs through magnetic dipole radiation and magnetic energy release. If asteroid-mass PBHs in the range $10^{-14}M_\odot$--$10^{-11}M_\odot$ constitute the dark matter, we estimate that searches of the Fermi-GBM archive and a future MeV gamma-ray mission such as COSI could detect these bursts. We also discuss possible multimessenger counterparts, including fast radio bursts powered by magnetic energy release, kilonovae and $511\,{\rm keV}$ line emission associated with centrifugally ejected neutron-rich matter, and gravitational waves from the rapid collapse and subsequent black-hole ringdown. Together, these signals probe complementary stages of PBH-induced NS consumption.

articles.title: First $Ω_{\rm m}-w$ Measurement Using Only Fast Radio Burst Observations
articles.abstract: Though fast radio bursts (FRBs) are widely advocated as a dark energy probe, no valid $Ω_m-w$ constraint has been obtained exclusively from FRB data to date. Benefiting from a rapidly growing localized sample and a novel statistical framework for modeling the dispersion measure (DM), we report the first simultaneous inference of the matter density $Ω_m$ and dark energy equation of state parameter $w$ from FRBs alone, without external observational priors on these two parameters. We combine a multi-parameter emulator for the nonlinear matter power spectrum with a physically motivated electron prescription to construct a cosmology-dependent cosmic-DM distribution. Within this unified analysis framework, the mean and variance of DM respond self-consistently to the same underlying cosmology, directly connecting the FRB likelihood to both cosmic expansion and structure growth. Analyzing 125 localized FRBs at $0.105\leq z\leq2.148$, we obtain $Ω_m = 0.33^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ and $w = -0.80^{+0.28}_{-0.38}$ under the flat $w$CDM model. We find a new positive $Ω_m-w$ degeneracy in the FRB posterior, opposite to the strong anticorrelation derived from Type Ia supernovae, offering a complementary test of dark energy properties and highlighting their potential in future precision cosmological studies.

articles.title: Dependence of Dust Growth on Magnetic field Strength in Protoplanetary Disks
articles.abstract: We performed one-dimensional calculations to investigate how the magnetorotational instability (MRI) affects dust growth in protoplanetary disks. We simultaneously solved the evolution of the dust size distribution and the vertical magnetic field. The dust size distribution is evolved taking into ac- count coagulation and fragmentation. For the magnetic field evolution, we considered both ambipolar diffusion and Ohmic dissipation. The MRI-driven turbulent viscosity was estimated self-consistently from the local magnetic field strength and non-ideal magnetohydrodynamics diffusivities. We found that MRI-driven turbulence becomes stronger for smaller initial plasma beta, and the enhanced tur- bulence promotes dust growth in MRI-active regions. However, dust growth is ultimately limited by radial drift, and the dependence of dust size on the magnetic field strength is significant only in the outer regions of the disk. In other words, over most of the disk, radial drift remains the dominant factor controlling the maximum dust size, and the magnetic field strength plays only a minor role in determining the overall dust size distribution.

articles.title: Anisotropic Coulomb Interaction in Strongly Magnetized Electron Gas at Zero Temperature in Relativistic Quantum Framework
articles.abstract: We present a microscopic derivation of Debye screening in a Landau-quantized electron gas subject to a strong magnetic field. By calculating the photon self-energy within the RPA framework, we explore how Landau levels influence the screening properties of the electron gas. Due to the quantum periodicity of Landau levels, the screening behavior is relatively insensitive to variations in the carrier density within each occupation cycle compared to the drastic changes induced by the magnetic field strength. Within a single occupation cycle, the Kohn anomaly dominates the low-density regime; at higher densities, its characteristic momentum shifts into the asymptotic high-momentum regime, rendering its singular contribution less prominent over the active screening domain and allowinga smooth orientation-dependent anisotropy to govern the system. Furthermore, a subtle competition in directional screening is observed between the parallel and perpendicular directions to the field depending on the density domain. At lower field strengths, multiple quantum oscillations emerge from the simultaneous participation of various Landau levels, marking a qualitative transition toward the isotropic three-dimensional limit. Our findings reveal anisotropic screening effects and provide insights into the behavior of charged impurities in such systems.

articles.title: Outflow Properties from a Broad Range of GR$ν$RMHD Stellar-Mass Black Hole Accretion Disks
articles.abstract: The majority of the mass ejected by neutron star mergers comes from accretion disk outflows. Over timescales of seconds, the thermodynamic evolution of the disk and its resultant outflows set the stage for the ejecta properties which manifest in kilonova observations at later times (hours/days). Kilonova observables depend sensitively on key properties of these outflows -- mass ejection, the ejecta velocity distribution, late-time ejecta morphology and nucleosynthetic yields -- which can only be modeled with a detailed treatment of microphysical interactions including neutrino and general relativistic effects. In this work, we present a library of 25 general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic accretion disks with neutrino transport, to our knowledge the largest to date, spanning a broad range of black hole and accretion disk combinations. From fits to our simulations, we derive analytic estimates of the average ejecta velocity distribution and mass ejection both at simulation end and extrapolated out to the end of the disk's lifetime. We also report ejecta morphology at timescales relevant to kilonova modeling, present spatially-dependent nucleosynthetic yields, and discuss the latter's dependence on initial disk conditions. While our disk library primarily includes initial conditions expected after neutron star mergers, a subset of our disks are applicable to other kilonova-adjacent scenarios.

articles.title: Multimessenger constraints on the origin of long gamma-ray bursts with plateaus: three cases
articles.abstract: The central engines of long gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) with X-ray plateaus remain uncertain. They involve a magnetar or black hole (BH), powered by spin energy and/or accretion. We examine how gravitational waves (GWs) discriminate between these scenarios. For collapsars, we consider three models: (A) a prompt phase powered by hyper-accretion onto a BH, followed by a spin-down-powered plateau; (B) a prompt phase powered by BH spin-down; and (C) a magnetar powering both the prompt and plateau phases. Each predicts a distinct GW signature in timing, energy, and frequency, ranging from broadband emission to a coherent descending chirp. We fit the selected X-ray plateaus of Swift GRBs using the model (A). For GRB~080319C, GRB~111209A, and GRB~130925A, we obtain BH masses of $M_{\rm BH}\sim24$--$124\,M_\odot$, with disc masses of $\sim10\%\,M_{\rm BH}$ at the end of the prompt phase. Mass-scaling of numerical simulations of disc emission yields GW strains of $\sim1.5-1.8\times10^{-24}$ at few hHz. This emission should be detectable by Cosmic Explorer and the Einstein Telescope, with an inferred rate from $0.5$ to $1.5$ yr$^{-1}$. However, ultra-long GRBs powered by tidal disruption events are expected to emit GWs at frequencies ranging from millihertz to decihertz, potentially within the sensitivity range of DECIGO and/or Big Bang Observer (BBO). Current or future detectors may detect GWs associated with BH-powered GRB, but magnetar engines, require next-generation detectors. Current and future detectors could map LGRB central-engine activity.

articles.title: New Candidate Activity Periods from FRB 20240209A and Repeating Fast Radio Burst Sources in the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog
articles.abstract: Repeating fast radio burst (FRB) sources with periodic activity provide important constraints on FRB models invoking neutron-star precession, rotation, or orbital modulation in binary systems. Although a few FRB sources exhibit evidence of periodic behavior, it remains unclear whether periodic activity is a common underlying feature of repeating FRBs. Using a new FRB periodicity search pipeline introduced by A. B. Pearlman et al. (2026), which is optimized for sparse event-arrival-time data from FRB surveys, we search for activity periods in the burst arrival times from FRB 20240209A and repeating FRBs in the Second Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME)/FRB Catalog. For FRB 20240209A, we identify a new candidate activity period of 170.4 $\pm$ 4.7 days, with a trials-corrected statistical significance of 5.3$σ$. Our larger burst sample shows no evidence of the 128.5-day activity period previously reported for this source by A. Pal (2025). We also report candidate activity periods of 28.46 $\pm$ 0.08 days, 86.7 $\pm$ 0.5 days, and 36.4 $\pm$ 0.5 days for FRB 20190208A, FRB 20200926A, and FRB 20220529A, with trials-corrected statistical significances of 3.1$σ$, 4.0$σ$, and 3.5$σ$, respectively. All statistical significances are evaluated against a homogeneous (constant-rate) Poisson null hypothesis, and we caution that they may decrease under null models that incorporate burst clustering. Collectively, our results constitute the most comprehensive search for periodic activity in the repeating FRB population to date.
